/-!
# Erdős Problem 281

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/281](https://www.erdosproblems.com/281)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [DaEr36] Davenport, H. and Erdős, P., *On sequences of positive integers*. Acta
  Arithmetica (1936), 147-151.
- [HaRo66] Halberstam, H. and Roth, K. F., *Sequences. Vol. I*. (1966), xx+291.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Topology

namespace Erdos281

/-- Choices of congruence classes $a_i \pmod{n_i}$. -/
def ResidueChoice (n : ℕ → ℕ) := ∀ i : ℕ, ZMod (n i)

/-- The integers avoiding all congruences $a_i \pmod{n_i}$. -/
def avoidAll (n : ℕ → ℕ) (a : ResidueChoice n) : Set ℤ :=
  {m | ∀ i : ℕ, (m : ZMod (n i)) ≠ a i}

/-- The integers avoiding the first $k$ congruences $a_i \pmod{n_i}$. -/
def avoidPrefix (n : ℕ → ℕ) (a : ResidueChoice n) (k : ℕ) : Set ℤ :=
  {m | ∀ i : ℕ, i < k → (m : ZMod (n i)) ≠ a i}

/--
Let $n_1<n_2<\cdots$ be an infinite sequence such that, for any choice of congruence classes
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$, the set of integers not satisfying any of the congruences $a_i\pmod{n_i}$ has
density $0$. Is it true that for every $\epsilon>0$ there exists some $k$ such that, for every
choice of congruence classes $a_i$, the density of integers not satisfying any of the congruences
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq k$ is less than $\epsilon$?

The answer is yes; the linked Lean proof formalizes Somani's argument.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos281.lean"]
theorem erdos_281 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono n → (∀ i, 0 < n i) →
      (∀ a : ResidueChoice n, Set.HasIntDensity (avoidAll n a) 0) →
        ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
          ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ a : ResidueChoice n,
            ∃ d : ℝ, Set.HasIntDensity (avoidPrefix n a k) d ∧ d < ε := by
  sorry

end Erdos281

reformulations.difference: Lean explicitly uses two-sided natural density on ℤ, counted in [-N,N], rather than the positive-integer density convention used in the cited density literature. This does not change this problem.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Write A(a) for the infinite avoidance set. Reflection gives -A(a) = A(-a), with residues negated coordinatewise. Since the hypothesis quantifies over every residue choice, one-sided density zero for every A(a) implies density zero on both half-lines and hence symmetric density zero. Conversely, symmetric density zero implies one-sided density zero by bounding the positive count by the symmetric count. For the conclusion, every finite-prefix avoidance set is periodic with positive period equal to the product (or lcm) of its finitely many positive moduli; its one-sided and symmetric densities therefore both exist and equal the same proportion of allowed residues. Thus the hypotheses and conclusions agree under either density convention.

review.notes:
All three definitions and the theorem agree with the original question on Erdős–Graham p. 29. The quantifier order preserves uniformity in residue choices, and answer(True) has the correct polarity. The status mirror agrees with research solved and the affirmative answer.

/workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully. Checks cover congruence semantics, nonempty residue-choice spaces, exclusion of modulus zero, the harmless modulus-one case, satisfiable hypotheses, density uniqueness, empty-prefix density 1, extension of finite residue choices, reflection, and positive-period periodicity. Small finite-prefix computations also behaved as expected. The full density-convention equivalence was not formalized.

The main erdosproblems.com page and forum returned Cloudflare 403 responses; the original cited book and the status mirror were used instead. Only the publicly available preview of Halberstam–Roth was accessible. The linked proof states exactly the required implication and contains no explicit proof holes or custom axioms, but its v4.29.1 proof could not be kernel-rechecked in the supplied v4.33.1 environment because of version/API incompatibilities; this is not evidence of a mathematical or status defect.
